338589.title: Zeta-polynomial conjecture for m-divisible odd noncrossing partitions
338589.review_depth: source conjecture text read in final version (sources/source-589.txt); follow-up Muhle-Nadeau-Williams arXiv:1904.05573 Theorem 1.3 and Section 8 read (sources/c-ar5iv-1904.05573.txt)
338589.notes: Conjecture 7.2 is equivalent to Z(ONC^{(m)}_{2n+1}, q) = Z(ONC_{2n+1}, m(q-1)+1), because MNW Theorem 1.3 (k=2, N=2n+1) gives Z(ONC,q'+1) = (q'+1)/(Nq'+1) binom(Nq'+n, n) and the identity C(a+1,n)/(a+1) = C(a,n)/(a+1-n) matches the conjectured formula. So the conjecture reduces to an Armstrong-type multichain transfer (Armstrong, Memoirs AMS 2009) for the order <=_3. A proof would very likely be a routine source-ingredient bridge (MNW Thm 1.3 plus Armstrong's argument), and a counterexample is implausible. Not pursued further. No computation.

338716.title: The classification conjecture for unsplittable cyclic (n_3) configurations
338716.review_depth: full source text read: Definitions 3-4, Theorems 6, 9, 10, 12, Table 1, Conjecture 1 (sources/source-716.txt). Web search found no follow-up.
338716.notes: MathDB paraphrases 'unsplittable' as 'neither point- nor line-splittable' (type T4). The source uses Definition 3 (no independent splitting set at all), and the source definition was used. Exact exhaustive DFS (claude-scripts/split.py): smallest component C containing 0+, Sigma = N(C) a 2-packing, 2|C|+|Sigma| <= 2n. It covers every girth-6 connected H(n,{0,a,b}) up to affine equivalence and reproduces columns (b), (e), (f) of the authors' Table 1 exactly for n = 7..30. Extended to n = 31..40 (beyond the authors' range): the unsplittable classes are exactly the three conjectured families, with no mismatch (outputs/claude-split/split-n7-20.json, split-n21-40.json). The 'only if' direction for all n is a long case analysis on non-generic symbols; not attempted.

338739.title: AMRZ conjecture on graph lines and universal pairs
338739.source: Matamala-Zamora arXiv:1803.07154v3; AMRZ Conjecture 2.3; Chvatal survey arXiv:1812.06288 Conjecture 5
338739.review_depth: source abstract; Chvatal survey Sections 3 and 3.7 read (sources/c-ar5iv-1812.06288.txt); web searches
338739.notes: Exhaustive check of lambda(G)+mu(G) >= |V| (line L(uv) = {w : d(u,v) = |d(u,w) +- d(w,v)|}). Canonically generated connected graphs on 2..8 vertices (1, 2, 6, 21, 112, 853, 11117, matching OEIS A001349; check-8: min slack 2). All 2,834,835 one-vertex extensions of the 11117 connected 8-vertex graphs cover every connected 9-vertex graph (each has a non-cut vertex): 0 violations, min slack 3. The fast implementation was cross-checked against a naive Floyd-Warshall version on 2584 graphs. Simulated annealing (diagnostic only) found min slack 3 at n=9 (equal to the exhaustive optimum) and 6 at n=12. Outputs: outputs/claude-amrz/. The growing slack suggests no small counterexample.

339077.title: The three-shifted q-Motzkin determinant conjecture
339077.source: Oh-Scrimshaw arXiv:1805.00113v1 (Discrete Math. 342 (2019)), Appendix A, Conjecture A.3
339077.review_depth: source Appendix A read (sources/source-077.txt); Omega A.2 certificate read; Cigler-Krattenthaler arXiv:2003.01676 text screened; registry screen; exact computations n <= 30
339077.notes: The printed statement is garbled: f_n is inherited from A.2, so the literal reading fails trivially at n=1 (misprint, not claimed). For the intended reading (det = (-1)^{floor(n/3)} q^{c_n} g_n, with the clause 'n = 2 mod 3 implies t_n | g_n'): at n = 5, the 5x5 integer Hankel matrix [M_{i+j+3}(-1)] has determinant 2, while t_5(-1) = 0, so t_5 cannot divide the cofactor. Refuted. Exact data for n <= 30: sign, nonnegativity and the n = 1 mod 3 formula hold; divisibility holds exactly for n = 2 mod 6 and fails for every n = 5 mod 6. A fitted complete closed form is verified for n <= 27 but unproved. Risk: first nontrivial instance (smallest-parameter or misprint correction), and the journal version could not be checked (ScienceDirect denied). See CANDIDATE.md (uncompiled Lean plan; certificate is one 5x5 integer determinant).

339156.title: Unique rectification targets in d-complete posets
339156.review_depth: source definitions read (Defs 2.8-2.15, URT definition, Conjecture 6.3, Lemma 6.4, Table 1; sources/c-ar5iv-1805.02287.txt); two web searches found no follow-up
339156.notes: Exhaustive K-jdt check (claude-scripts/urt.py), with slides into every nonempty set of inner corners and all slide sequences. Every skew increasing tableau inside P with label set {1..h}, h <= height(P), was tested for having a minimally labelled rectification and also another rectification. Posets: heaps of lambda-minuscule elements (lambda a fundamental weight) for star Dynkin diagrams with arms up to (1,1,6), (1,2,6), (1,3,4), (2,2,4), (2,3,3), at every node. These are d-complete (Proctor), and Proctor's dualised axioms were also checked directly. All 288 non-isomorphic maximal heaps of size <= 11 were tested, covering 4,565,120 tableaux: 2373 have several rectifications, and 0 violate the conjecture. Control: the 3x3 rectangle shows multi-rectification tableaux but no violation. Outputs: outputs/claude-urt/.
